findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `I18n.ensure_loaded! l` assumes the TranslateAccelerator module has been extended into the I18n module itself, but the diff only adds `ensure_loaded!` as an instance method on the backend in translate_accelerator.rb and shows no `I18n.extend(TranslateAccelerator)` anywhere in this change. If the extension is not present elsewhere in the pre-existing tree, every request that reaches set_locale raises NoMethodError (undefined method `ensure_loaded!` for I18n module), turning the whole site into 500s; the feasibility of this initializer rests on an unverifiable out-of-diff assumption.

[ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale eagerly on every fallback lookup, so any I18n translate with fallbacks triggered before the database is connected (boot-time initializers, assets:precompile on a machine without the DB, early rake tasks) executes a SiteSetting read against a missing connection. Operators running `rake assets:precompile` or bootstrap tasks on a fresh checkout without a migrated DB get an uninitialized-constant/connection error from a config-time lookup that previously (config.i18n.fallbacks = true) never touched SiteSetting.

[ADVISORY] set_locale calls `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` unconditionally on every request, but fallbacks are now only configured by config/initializers/i18n.rb — if that initializer is loaded in an environment where I18n.fallbacks is nil or Rails has reset it (e.g. a Rails engine or test harness re-assigning I18n.backend/fallbacks), this raises NoMethodError on nil. Any environment or spec that reloads I18n configuration after initializers (common in test suites and plugin specs that reset I18n) crashes every controller request at set_locale with NoMethodError on nil.ensure_loaded!.

[ADVISORY] TranslateAccelerator#ensure_loaded! reads `@loaded_locales` with `||=` but the existing translate path (line 67) calls `@loaded_locales.include?` without that nil guard, and the new method silently diverges from load_locale's own bookkeeping — the two sites now maintain the same lazy-init invariant by hand. The next change to locale-loading bookkeeping must be applied in two places; if only one is updated, ensure_loaded! either re-loads locales every request (perf regression) or skips loading a locale that was evicted from @loaded_locales, producing untranslated strings. Safe to collapse by having translate call ensure_loaded!.

[ADVISORY] The new fallback chain is only wired into the request path via ensure_loaded! in ApplicationController#set_locale, so server-side translation consumers outside the request cycle (Sidekiq jobs, ActionMailer previews/deliveries, rake tasks, onebox rendering in background) silently get no fallback loading. Emails and background-job strings rendered in a user locale with missing keys fall back to a locale the TranslateAccelerator never loaded, yielding missing/blank translations exactly on the paths the feature name ("server-side") promises to cover; no spec in this diff exercises a non-request rendering path.

[ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList#[] reads SiteSetting.default_locale on every fallback-chain construction, coupling every I18n lookup (a hot path) to the SiteSetting store and to a connected database. Any code performing translations before the DB/Redis setting store is available (asset precompile, db:create during bootstrap, early initializers) raises, and every translate call in production pays an extra settings lookup; the diff contains no test or guard for lookup-before-DB contexts.

[ADVISORY] set_locale calls I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!, but the i18n gem defines no module-level I18n.ensure_loaded!(locale); only the custom TranslateAccelerator backend defines ensure_loaded!, and the diff shows no delegate added on the I18n module. If no such delegation exists elsewhere, every request raises NoMethodError on I18n.ensure_loaded! in set_locale, a hard 500 on all pages; if a delegate does exist it is out-of-diff and unverified here — either way the diff ships the call with no spec asserting it runs.

[ADVISORY] The new global fallback behavior has no tests anywhere in the diff — no spec file covers FallbackLocaleList ordering, uniq/compact behavior, or the ensure_loaded! path. A regression in fallback order (e.g. duplicate locales, nil default_locale, non-symbol locale keys) ships undetected; the diff deletes the old environment-scoped fallback config (production.rb, profile.rb, cloud66) while adding behavior-bearing logic with zero verification, including no test that removing config.i18n.fallbacks from those environments preserves prior behavior in them.

[ADVISORY] TranslateAccelerator#ensure_loaded! does not record the locale in @loaded_locales, delegating to load_locale — but load_locale's append behavior is out-of-diff and the existing translate path checks @loaded_locales.include?(config.locale) directly, so a mismatch would make ensure_loaded! a repeated no-op or infinite reload. If load_locale does not push onto @loaded_locales for a locale already half-loaded (partial translations), repeated per-request ensure_loaded! calls re-parse locale files, and no test in the diff pins this contract.

[BUG] FallbackLocaleList overrides Hash#[] to always compute a fresh array, so any external write to the fallbacks map becomes a silent no-op. Code that configures fallbacks via the standard I18n API (e.g. `I18n.fallbacks[:de] = [:de, :en]` from a plugin, admin setting, or spec setup) stores the entry via []=, but the overridden [] never reads stored values — every subsequent lookup silently ignores the configured fallback chain and returns the hard-coded [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en] instead.

[ADVISORY] ensure_loaded! runs unconditionally at the end of set_locale on every request, including requests whose locale was already loaded in a previous request within the same process. Every request in production pays FallbackLocaleList#[] construction (a SiteSetting.default_locale read plus array build plus uniq) plus a hash traversal of up to three locales before hitting the @loaded_locales.include? short-circuit inside TranslateAccelerator; operators of high-traffic instances get a measurable per-request cost on a hot path the diff did not previously touch.

[ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList#[] performs a SiteSetting read on every single translation lookup rather than caching per locale, duplicating work that a Hash with a default_proc would memoize. Background jobs, serializers, and any code that translates strings outside the controller set_locale path call I18n.fallbacks[locale] through the backend on every t() call; each such call re-reads SiteSetting.default_locale and rebuilds the array, so heavy translation consumers in worker processes pay the cost thousands of times per job.

[BUG] ensure_loaded! is only invoked from ApplicationController#set_locale, so fallback locales are never loaded on any non-request path (background jobs, Sidekiq mailers, scheduled tasks, console-rendered emails). With config.i18n.fallbacks removed from production.rb and replaced by FallbackLocaleList, a Sidekiq job rendering a localized email for locale :fr falls back to :en, but the TranslateAccelerator backend has only loaded :fr (translate calls load_locale(config.locale) alone), so the :en fallback lookup misses and the email ships raw translation keys / missing-translation spans; the fallback feature silently works only for web requests.

[ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but overrides #[] to compute values dynamically, so any code that writes into or reads from it as a real Hash gets silently ignored values. If any code path (plugin, future core change, or the I18n gem's Fallbacks module itself, which allows per-locale fallback mutation like I18n.fallbacks[:de] = [:de_DE]) stores an entry, the stored value is unreachable because #[] never reads the underlying hash — a silent no-op configuration that looks set but isn't. The next maintainer extending fallbacks per the TODO comment will write into this hash and it will do nothing.

[ADVISORY] Removing config.i18n.fallbacks = true and installing the custom fallback list via an initializer changes fallback behavior in development and test environments, which never enabled fallbacks before. Developers running test suites or local dev servers previously saw untranslated/missing keys surface as failures for incomplete locales; now every locale silently falls back to :en (and SiteSetting.default_locale), so missing-translation regressions in non-English locale files are masked exactly where they'd be caught, while production-only differences (e.g. default_locale-derived fallback chains depending on per-site settings) behave differently between dev and prod.

[ADVISORY] ensure_loaded! guards with @loaded_locales.include?(locale) but load_locale already performs the same check internally, and @loaded_locales is lazily initialized to [] only in this new method while translate() dereferences it unconditionally, coupling the new method to load_locale's internal bookkeeping. The duplication means a future change to load_locale's tracking (e.g. switching @loaded_locales to a Set or renaming it) silently breaks ensure_loaded!'s guard; also the lazy `||= []` in one method and bare use in the other means any new caller of ensure_loaded! before translate() works only by accident of the ordering — a change-safety hazard rather than a present crash.

[ADVISORY] The new fallback chain silently changes the accepted localization contract from 'fall back to the default locale when a translation cannot be found' (the exact wording deleted from production.rb/profile.rb/cloud66 production.rb) to 'fall back to SiteSetting.default_locale, then always to English'. Operators of sites whose default_locale is non-English and whose default-locale translations are incomplete now get raw English strings where the previous config.i18n.fallbacks = true setup returned the missing-translation marker (since the old fallback target was the site default itself); this broadened objective was never explicitly accepted — the PR title only promises 'fallbacks', not a hardwired English terminal fallback. Bitten: every non-English-default site immediately after deploy.

[BUG] FallbackLocaleList#[] performs a SiteSetting.default_locale read on every I18n fallback resolution, coupling translation lookups to the settings store in contexts where SiteSetting is not safely reachable (rake tasks, migrations, and console during first boot before the settings table exists), raising NoMethodError/NameError inside I18n instead of returning a translation. Any background job, migration, or script that resolves a translation with a missing key before the site settings are loadable crashes with an I18n-internal error rather than the previous deterministic Rails-fallback behavior (config.i18n.fallbacks = true, a pure in-memory lookup with no dependency on the database).

[ADVISORY] The initializer carries an undocumented-by-machinery load-order dependency ("# order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb") with no runtime guard that TranslateAccelerator has actually been mixed into I18n.backend yet. If freedom_patches load order changes (or an eager-load/require sequence change in a future deploy), I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! in ApplicationController#set_locale calls a backend method that does not exist and every request 500s at boot-of-first-request; nothing in the diff enforces the ordering it depends on.

[ADVISORY] Removing config.i18n.fallbacks = true from the Cloud66-managed production.rb couples a separately-deployed config file to a code-shipped initializer for fallback behavior. Operators whose Cloud66 stack applies files/production.rb on a different schedule than the code deploy get a window where fallbacks are disabled entirely (old config removed, new initializer not yet on the box), so untranslated strings render as missing-translation keys instead of falling back to the default locale.

[ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but its [] ignores all stored state, so any explicit per-locale fallback configuration written into I18n.fallbacks (the mechanism the Hash superclass exists to support) is silently discarded and replaced by [locale, default_locale, :en]. A developer or plugin that sets I18n.fallbacks[:de] = [:de_AT, :en] per the i18n gem's documented API gets no error and no effect — every lookup silently uses the hardcoded chain; the inheritance from Hash invites exactly the misuse it cannot honor.

[ADVISORY] Every fallback-chain computation performs SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym inside Hash#[], which runs on the per-translation-miss hot path of I18n::Backend::Fallbacks (the backend calls fallbacks[locale] for each translation that misses). Any code path where SiteSetting is unavailable or uncached (background jobs, one-off rake tasks before Rails full boot, multisite with no current site) raises NoMethodError on nil.to_sym inside translation lookup, turning a cosmetic missing translation into a hard failure.

[ADVISORY] The new ensure_loaded! guard reads @loaded_locales.include?(locale) after only lazily initializing it with ||= [], while the pre-existing translate() method guards with a separate pattern — two parallel load-state checks that can drift. A future edit to how @loaded_locales is reset (e.g., a cache-flush that nils it) makes ensure_loaded! the only safe caller while translate()'s pattern crashes or double-loads; the duplication makes the next change to locale-loading riskier because two sites must be updated in lockstep.

[ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList#[] invokes SiteSetting.default_locale on every fallback lookup, coupling every translation miss in every process (mailers, background jobs, migrations, asset precompile) to the settings store. Any code path that translates before the SiteSetting cache/DB is available (e.g., a translation miss raised during db:migrate or rake asset:precompile, where fallbacks are now enabled globally by this initializer in all environments) hits SiteSetting before Rails is ready and raises, turning a previously harmless untranslated key into a boot/task failure; operators get bitten during deploys and maintenance tasks.

[ADVISORY] ensure_loaded! uses an unsynchronized check-then-act on the shared @loaded_locales array, so concurrent first requests for the same locale both execute load_locale. Under the first burst of traffic after a process restart, multiple threads simultaneously parse and register the same locale files (duplicated file reads and backend reload work), adding avoidable latency spikes on the hot request path; behavior is eventually consistent so no user-visible data corruption, but the guard does not actually guard.

[ADVISORY] I18n.fallbacks is assigned before the accelerator backend's fallback-augmented translate path is exercised, and FallbackLocaleList#[] re-reads SiteSetting.default_locale on every call rather than memoizing per user-locale, so every translation miss triggers a fresh settings lookup plus array/uniq allocation. Sites with any untranslated key pay a SiteSetting cache read and array construction per miss per request; on high-traffic multilingual instances this is a measurable hot-path regression versus the previous static default_locale fallback chain that Rails configured once at boot.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

This is a concrete performance/architecture concern grounded in the diff, not a correctness bug.

With config.i18n.fallbacks removed from production.rb and replaced by FallbackLocaleList, a Sidekiq job rendering a localized email for locale :fr falls back to :en, but the TranslateAccelerator backend has only loaded :fr (translate calls load_locale(config.locale) alone), so the :en fallback lookup misses and the email ships raw translation keys / missing-translation spans; the fallback feature silently works only for web requests.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces explicit preloading of fallback locales via `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` in `ApplicationController#set_locale`, while removing `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from environment configs. The new fallback loader (`FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!`) is only triggered on the web request path (controller). Meanwhile, the `TranslateAccelerator` backend still lazy-loads only `config.locale` in `translate` (`load_locale(config.locale) unless @loaded_locales.include?(config.locale)`), and nothing in the diff shows equivalent fallback-locale preloading for non-controller execution (jobs, mailers, console). This makes it plausible/likely that fallback translations won’t be loaded outside requests, yielding missing translations when fallbacks are used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but overrides #[] to compute values dynamically, so any code that writes into or reads from it as a real Hash gets silently ignored values. If any code path (plugin, future core change, or the I18n gem's Fallbacks module itself, which allows per-locale fallback mutation like I18n.fallbacks[:de] = [:de_DE]) stores an entry, the stored value is unreachable because #[] never reads the underlying hash — a silent no-op configuration that looks set but isn't. The next maintainer extending fallbacks per the TODO comment will write into this hash and it will do nothing.

adjudication.rationale: In `config/initializers/i18n.rb`, `FallbackLocaleList < Hash` overrides `#[]` to always return a computed array and never calls `super`, so any values stored into the underlying hash (e.g., via `I18n.fallbacks[:de] = ...` or `fallbacks.store`) would never be read back. The diff itself doesn’t show any current write path, so it’s not a currently verifiable runtime bug, but it is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/extension hazard (reinforced by the adjacent TODO about extending per-language fallbacks).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Removing config.i18n.fallbacks = true and installing the custom fallback list via an initializer changes fallback behavior in development and test environments, which never enabled fallbacks before. Developers running test suites or local dev servers previously saw untranslated/missing keys surface as failures for incomplete locales; now every locale silently falls back to :en (and SiteSetting.default_locale), so missing-translation regressions in non-English locale files are masked exactly where they'd be caught, while production-only differences (e.g. default_locale-derived fallback chains depending on per-site settings) behave differently between dev and prod.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from specific environment configs (production/profile/cloud66) and replaces it with a global initializer `config/initializers/i18n.rb` that mixes in `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` and sets `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new` with a `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]` chain. Since initializers run in all environments unless guarded, this change plausibly enables fallbacks in development/test too, altering how missing translations surface (potentially masking missing keys locally vs previously). This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral scope change, but not an objectively broken behavior by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ensure_loaded! guards with @loaded_locales.include?(locale) but load_locale already performs the same check internally, and @loaded_locales is lazily initialized to [] only in this new method while translate() dereferences it unconditionally, coupling the new method to load_locale's internal bookkeeping. The duplication means a future change to load_locale's tracking (e.g. switching @loaded_locales to a Set or renaming it) silently breaks ensure_loaded!'s guard; also the lazy `||= []` in one method and bare use in the other means any new caller of ensure_loaded! before translate() works only by accident of the ordering — a change-safety hazard rather than a present crash.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ensure_loaded!(locale)` in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` which directly manipulates `@loaded_locales` (`@loaded_locales ||= []` and `include?`), while `translate()` (existing code) dereferences `@loaded_locales` without initialization. This creates tighter coupling to the internal tracking variable and its shape/name, making future refactors of locale tracking more fragile. However, the finding’s claim that `load_locale` already performs the same guard can’t be verified from the provided diff, and there is no new, definite runtime break shown (translate’s uninitialized deref existed before).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new fallback chain silently changes the accepted localization contract from 'fall back to the default locale when a translation cannot be found' (the exact wording deleted from production.rb/profile.rb/cloud66 production.rb) to 'fall back to SiteSetting.default_locale, then always to English'. Operators of sites whose default_locale is non-English and whose default-locale translations are incomplete now get raw English strings where the previous config.i18n.fallbacks = true setup returned the missing-translation marker (since the old fallback target was the site default itself); this broadened objective was never explicitly accepted — the PR title only promises 'fallbacks', not a hardwired English terminal fallback. Bitten: every non-English-default site immediately after deploy.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a hardwired terminal English fallback: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` returns `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]` and assigns it via `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new` (config/initializers/i18n.rb). This replaces the prior `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` settings removed from multiple env configs, so the fallback chain semantics are materially broadened in a way not reflected elsewhere in the diff. However, claims about the exact previous runtime outcome (e.g., always showing the missing-translation marker vs English, and immediate operator impact) are not fully verifiable from this diff alone because it depends on how `I18n.default_locale`/SiteSetting are wired and what translations exist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] FallbackLocaleList#[] performs a SiteSetting.default_locale read on every I18n fallback resolution, coupling translation lookups to the settings store in contexts where SiteSetting is not safely reachable (rake tasks, migrations, and console during first boot before the settings table exists), raising NoMethodError/NameError inside I18n instead of returning a translation. Any background job, migration, or script that resolves a translation with a missing key before the site settings are loadable crashes with an I18n-internal error rather than the previous deterministic Rails-fallback behavior (config.i18n.fallbacks = true, a pure in-memory lookup with no dependency on the database).

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a custom `FallbackLocaleList#[]` in `config/initializers/i18n.rb` that always includes `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` in the fallback chain (`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`). This is a new coupling of I18n fallback resolution to `SiteSetting`, and `#[]` is invoked as part of I18n fallback lookups. While the diff alone can’t prove `SiteSetting.default_locale` will crash in rake tasks/migrations/first-boot, the dependency and repeated settings read on every fallback resolution is real and could be problematic in non-fully-bootstrapped contexts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The initializer carries an undocumented-by-machinery load-order dependency ("# order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb") with no runtime guard that TranslateAccelerator has actually been mixed into I18n.backend yet. If freedom_patches load order changes (or an eager-load/require sequence change in a future deploy), I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! in ApplicationController#set_locale calls a backend method that does not exist and every request 500s at boot-of-first-request; nothing in the diff enforces the ordering it depends on.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an explicit load-order dependency in `config/initializers/i18n.rb` via the comment `# order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb`, and adds a new runtime call site `ApplicationController#set_locale` -> `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`. There is no runtime guard/check that whatever defines/installs `ensure_loaded!` (likely related to the `TranslateAccelerator` change in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb`) has been applied before requests hit `set_locale`. Rails’ initializer filename ordering may make this work today, but the dependency is not enforced or asserted in code, so the finding’s core concern (fragile ordering with a potential hard failure if ordering changes) is diff-grounded, though the exact failure mode is somewhat speculative from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Removing config.i18n.fallbacks = true from the Cloud66-managed production.rb couples a separately-deployed config file to a code-shipped initializer for fallback behavior. Operators whose Cloud66 stack applies files/production.rb on a different schedule than the code deploy get a window where fallbacks are disabled entirely (old config removed, new initializer not yet on the box), so untranslated strings render as missing-translation keys instead of falling back to the default locale.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from both `config/environments/production.rb` and the Cloud66-managed `config/cloud/cloud66/files/production.rb`, while introducing fallback behavior via a new code-shipped initializer (`config/initializers/i18n.rb` sets `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new` and includes `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks`). This does create a coordination/operational coupling between an externally managed env file and application code: if those artifacts are deployed on different schedules, fallback behavior could differ between versions. The claim about a specific window where fallbacks are “disabled entirely” depends on deployment mechanics not shown in the diff, so it’s not a verifiable code defect, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded ops/rollout concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but its [] ignores all stored state, so any explicit per-locale fallback configuration written into I18n.fallbacks (the mechanism the Hash superclass exists to support) is silently discarded and replaced by [locale, default_locale, :en]. A developer or plugin that sets I18n.fallbacks[:de] = [:de_AT, :en] per the i18n gem's documented API gets no error and no effect — every lookup silently uses the hardcoded chain; the inheritance from Hash invites exactly the misuse it cannot honor.

adjudication.rationale: In `config/initializers/i18n.rb`, `FallbackLocaleList < Hash` overrides `[]` to always return `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`, ignoring any values that might be stored in the underlying Hash via `I18n.fallbacks[:de] = ...`. Since the diff sets `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new`, any code expecting the documented hash-like per-locale configuration would be silently ineffective. The diff doesn’t show such callers, so it’s an API/compatibility/design concern rather than a verifiable runtime defect in this PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Every fallback-chain computation performs SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym inside Hash#[], which runs on the per-translation-miss hot path of I18n::Backend::Fallbacks (the backend calls fallbacks[locale] for each translation that misses). Any code path where SiteSetting is unavailable or uncached (background jobs, one-off rake tasks before Rails full boot, multisite with no current site) raises NoMethodError on nil.to_sym inside translation lookup, turning a cosmetic missing translation into a hard failure.

adjudication.rationale: The new `FallbackLocaleList#[]` unconditionally does `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` for every fallback lookup (`config/initializers/i18n.rb`), which `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` will consult repeatedly on missing translations. That introduces a dependency on `SiteSetting` being available/initialized on the translation lookup path and could add overhead. However, from the diff alone we can’t verify that `SiteSetting.default_locale` can be `nil` (or unavailable) in any execution mode, so the claimed hard failure (`nil.to_sym`) is not provable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new ensure_loaded! guard reads @loaded_locales.include?(locale) after only lazily initializing it with ||= [], while the pre-existing translate() method guards with a separate pattern — two parallel load-state checks that can drift. A future edit to how @loaded_locales is reset (e.g., a cache-flush that nils it) makes ensure_loaded! the only safe caller while translate()'s pattern crashes or double-loads; the duplication makes the next change to locale-loading riskier because two sites must be updated in lockstep.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb the new ensure_loaded!(locale) initializes @loaded_locales with ||= [] before checking include?, while the existing translate method still does `load_locale(config.locale) unless @loaded_locales.include?(config.locale)` without any local initialization. This creates two inconsistent load-state guard patterns in the same class, increasing maintenance risk (future changes to how @loaded_locales is initialized/reset would need to be kept in sync). The diff does not show a concrete crash today, but the duplication/inconsistency is real and introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] FallbackLocaleList#[] invokes SiteSetting.default_locale on every fallback lookup, coupling every translation miss in every process (mailers, background jobs, migrations, asset precompile) to the settings store. Any code path that translates before the SiteSetting cache/DB is available (e.g., a translation miss raised during db:migrate or rake asset:precompile, where fallbacks are now enabled globally by this initializer in all environments) hits SiteSetting before Rails is ready and raises, turning a previously harmless untranslated key into a boot/task failure; operators get bitten during deploys and maintenance tasks.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a global initializer (config/initializers/i18n.rb) that enables I18n fallbacks in all environments by including I18n::Backend::Fallbacks and setting I18n.fallbacks to FallbackLocaleList. FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale on each lookup (`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`), which does couple fallback resolution to SiteSetting. However, the claim that this will definitively raise during tasks like db:migrate/asset:precompile is not directly verifiable from the diff (it depends on how/when SiteSetting is available and when translations are invoked). It is still a concrete, diff-grounded architectural/edge-case concern introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ensure_loaded! uses an unsynchronized check-then-act on the shared @loaded_locales array, so concurrent first requests for the same locale both execute load_locale. Under the first burst of traffic after a process restart, multiple threads simultaneously parse and register the same locale files (duplicated file reads and backend reload work), adding avoidable latency spikes on the hot request path; behavior is eventually consistent so no user-visible data corruption, but the guard does not actually guard.
matched_golden_ids: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same concurrency flaw: @loaded_locales is a shared, lazily-populated structure accessed via an unsynchronized check-then-act pattern, allowing multiple threads to concurrently load/register the same locale.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] I18n.fallbacks is assigned before the accelerator backend's fallback-augmented translate path is exercised, and FallbackLocaleList#[] re-reads SiteSetting.default_locale on every call rather than memoizing per user-locale, so every translation miss triggers a fresh settings lookup plus array/uniq allocation. Sites with any untranslated key pay a SiteSetting cache read and array construction per miss per request; on high-traffic multilingual instances this is a measurable hot-path regression versus the previous static default_locale fallback chain that Rails configured once at boot.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a custom `FallbackLocaleList#[]` that recomputes `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` on every access (config/initializers/i18n.rb), so the concern about repeated `SiteSetting.default_locale` reads and array/`uniq` allocations is grounded. Whether this happens specifically “per translation miss” and whether it’s a measurable regression versus previous Rails boot-time fallback configuration is plausible but not directly verifiable from the diff alone; however, the repeated computation/hot-path risk created by this change is a concrete non-bug review issue.
